items.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021
items.q: Lee had me singing Lester Young solos and Louis Armstrong.

ctx.x: Would you ever, during an improvised solo on a standard tune, would you ever play a snippet of the melody perhaps, to remind the audience here’s where we are, or something like that?

Yeah sometimes, and some tunes just to remind myself too, to get back to see where I am. And I think keeping the melody close is very important. And also it’s a reference point and if you can develop that, you know Lee Konitz had this kind of one to ten thing where if you’re playing the melody that’s number one and if you’re playing something that’s totally unlike the melody, you know if you’re playing bebop maybe that’s number five or number six. If you’re playing really abstractly that’s number ten, but you’re…
like let it be, you know like especially if you’ve got great players playing with you, you know you can lean on that. And sometimes we don’t.
